facts.statement: Scipionyx lived in Italy during the Early Cretaceous, approximately 113 million years ago.
facts.quote: Scipionyx ( ) was a genus of theropod dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous Pietraroja Formation of Italy, around 113 million years ago.

facts.statement: Only one fossil of Scipionyx is known, discovered in 1981 and brought to scientific attention in 1993.
facts.quote: There is only one fossil known of Scipionyx, discovered in 1981 by an amateur paleontologist and brought to the attention of science in 1993.

facts.statement: The Scipionyx fossil is famous for preserving large areas of petrified soft tissue, including muscles and intestines.
facts.quote: The find generated much publicity because of the unique preservation of large areas of petrified soft tissue and internal organs such as muscles and intestines.

facts.statement: Scipionyx was the first dinosaur discovered in Italy.
facts.quote: It was also the first dinosaur found in Italy.

facts.statement: Scipionyx was discovered in 1981 by amateur paleontologist Giovanni Todesco in the Le Cavere quarry near Pietraroja, Italy.
facts.quote: Scipionyx was discovered in the spring of 1981 by Giovanni Todesco, an amateur paleontologist, in the small Le Cavere quarry at the edge of the village of Pietraroja, approximately seventy kilometers northeast of Naples.

facts.statement: The species Scipionyx samniticus was named and described in 1998 by Marco Signore and Cristiano Dal Sasso.
facts.quote: In 1998, Ciro because of this made the front cover of Nature, when the type species Scipionyx samniticus was named and described by Marco Signore and Cristiano Dal Sasso.

facts.statement: The genus name Scipionyx means "Scipio's claw".
facts.quote: The generic name Scipionyx comes from the Latin name Scipio and the Greek ὄνυξ, onyx, the combination meaning "Scipio's claw".

facts.statement: The known fossil of Scipionyx is a juvenile approximately 46.1 cm long, possibly only three days old.
facts.quote: The fossil is that of a juvenile that was most likely a baby, at only 46.1 cm long, and perhaps just three days old.

facts.statement: The adult form and size of Scipionyx are unknown.
facts.quote: Its adult form and size is unknown.

facts.statement: Scipionyx was a bipedal predator with a long tail that balanced its horizontal rump.
facts.quote: Scipionyx was a bipedal predator, its horizontal rump balanced by a long tail.

facts.statement: Scipionyx likely had primitive feathers, though no skin or feather remains have been found in the fossil.
facts.quote: Its body was probably covered by primitive feathers but these have not been found in the fossil, that is without any skin remains.

facts.statement: Half-digested remains of lizards and fish found in the fossil indicate Scipionyx ate these animals.
facts.quote: In the guts of the fossil some half-digested meals are still present, indicating Scipionyx ate lizards and fish.

facts.statement: Scientists disagree on how Scipionyx breathed based on the position of its internal organs.
facts.quote: Several scientists have tried to learn from the position of the internal organs how Scipionyx breathed, but their conclusions often disagree.

facts.statement: The preserved length of the Scipionyx holotype is estimated at 23.7 cm.
facts.quote: The holotype of Scipionyx represents a very small individual, the preserved length of which is estimated at just 23.7 cm.

facts.statement: In 2011, researchers estimated the total length of Scipionyx, including the missing tail, at 46.1 cm.
facts.quote: In 2011, dal Sasso and Maganuco estimated its total length, including the missing tail section, at 46.1 cm.

facts.statement: Scipionyx had a long slender neck, elongated hindlimbs, and especially elongated forelimbs.
facts.quote: Scipionyx was a small bipedal predator. Its horizontal rump was balanced by a long tail. The neck was relatively long and slender. The hindlimbs and especially the forelimbs were rather elongated.

facts.statement: A 2011 study identified eight unique derived traits distinguishing Scipionyx from its closest relatives.
facts.quote: The 2011 study established eight unique derived traits or autapomorphies in which Scipionyx differed from its closest relatives.

facts.statement: The first finger of Scipionyx is 23% longer than the third finger.
facts.quote: The first finger is conspicuously elongated, 23% longer than the third finger.

facts.statement: The holotype skull is large relative to the body, short, and features very large eye-sockets.
facts.quote: The skull of the holotype is large, compared to the size of the body, and short with very large eye-sockets.

facts.statement: The premaxilla bone carries five teeth.
facts.quote: The premaxilla, the bone forming the front of the snout, carries five teeth.

facts.statement: The maxilla is deep with a short front branch and carries seven teeth.
facts.quote: The maxilla behind it, is deep with a very short front branch. It carries seven teeth.

facts.statement: The animal has a total of forty-four teeth in the head, with twenty-two on each side.
facts.quote: Scipionyx has five teeth in the premaxilla, seven in the maxilla and ten in the dentary of the lower jaw for a total of twenty-two per side and a grand total for the head of forty-four.

facts.statement: Having five premaxillary teeth is surprising because four is normal for compsognathids, and five is only found in some Carnosauria.
facts.quote: The number of five premaxillary teeth is surprising, as a total of four is normal for compsognathids: otherwise, only some Carnosauria have five.

facts.statement: The teeth generally curve gradually rather than having the typical sudden recurving apex, though the largest teeth show a slight kink.
facts.quote: The teeth lack the typical compsognathid shape with a suddenly recurving apex of the tooth crown. Instead, in general they curve gradually; only the largest teeth show something of a "kink".

facts.statement: Exceptionally, the lower jaw tooth row extends further back than the upper jaw tooth row.
facts.quote: Exceptionally, the tooth row of the lower jaw extends further to the back than that of the upper jaw.

facts.statement: The maxillary teeth are flattened and have denticles on their trailing edges.
facts.quote: The maxillary teeth are flattened with denticles on their trailing edges.

facts.statement: The second and fifth premaxillary teeth are the largest in that row.
facts.quote: The second and fifth teeth are the largest.

facts.statement: The fourth maxillary tooth is the largest tooth of the entire head.
facts.quote: The second and fourth maxillary teeth are the largest; the latter being the largest tooth of all.

facts.statement: A diamond-shaped fontanelle exists on the skull roof where bones have not yet closed, a feature initially mistaken for preparation damage.
facts.quote: The skull roof over a limited distance has not closed yet, resulting in a conspicuous diamond-shaped opening, a fontanelle that was first mistaken for damage inflicted on the fossil during the first preparation.

facts.statement: The lower jaw is straight and elongated.
facts.quote: The lower jaw is straight and elongated.

facts.statement: Because the specimen was young and had not started its tooth replacement cycle, the left and right jaws showed perfect dental symmetry.
facts.quote: Due to the young age of the specimen, the tooth replacement cycle had not started yet, causing a perfect dental symmetry between the left and the right jaws.

facts.statement: The vertebral column of Scipionyx likely contained ten cervical vertebrae and thirteen dorsal vertebrae.

facts.quote: With certainty five sacral vertebrae are present

facts.quote: The fossil has preserved just nine tail vertebrae; likely fifty or more had been originally present

facts.statement: The neck vertebrae of Scipionyx are opisthocoelous.
facts.quote: The neck vertebrae are opisthocoelous

facts.quote: The axis is pneumatised as a pneumatopore

facts.quote: Contrary to what was stated by the 1998 study, the cervical ribs are very elongated, with a length of up to three vertebral centra

facts.statement: Scipionyx possessed at least twelve pairs of dorsal ribs.
facts.quote: There are at least twelve pairs of dorsal ribs

facts.quote: The lower rump is covered by a basket of eighteen pairs of gastralia or belly ribs

facts.statement: The gastralia of Scipionyx form a herringbone pattern.
facts.quote: The gastralia form a herringbone pattern

facts.quote: The furcula is broad and more or less U-shaped with its two branches angled at 125°

facts.statement: The ulna of Scipionyx is slender, cylinder-shaped, and 70% the length of the humerus.
facts.quote: The ulna is slender and cylinder-shaped with a length of 70% of that of the humerus

facts.statement: The third finger of Scipionyx is exceptionally long for a compsognathid, measuring 123% of the thumb length.
facts.quote: The third finger is exceptionally long for a comspognathid, with 123% of thumb length

facts.statement: The ilium of Scipionyx is short, flat, and has a slightly convex upper profile.
facts.quote: The ilium is short and flat with a slightly convex upper profile

facts.quote: The pubic bone points almost vertically downwards and is thus "mesopubic" or "orthopubic"

facts.statement: The ischium of Scipionyx is three-quarters the length of the pubis and is set at a 54-degree angle to it.
facts.quote: The ischium has three quarters the length of the pubis, set at an angle of 54° to it

facts.statement: Scipionyx is unique among dinosaurs for preserving examples from most major internal organ groups, including blood, cartilage, muscle, and the respiratory and digestive systems.
facts.quote: Scipionyx is unique in preserving in some form examples from most major internal organ groups: blood, blood vessels, cartilage, connective tissues, bone tissue, muscle tissue, horn sheaths, the respiratory system and the digestive system

facts.statement: The soft tissues in Scipionyx are preserved as three-dimensional petrifications rather than as imprints.
facts.quote: The soft tissues are not present in the form of imprints but as three-dimensional petrifications

facts.statement: Although original bone tissue is gone, calcium phosphate mineralization in Scipionyx preserved the structure of original bone cells.
facts.quote: The original bone tissue is no longer present but the calcium phosphate mineralisation has preserved the structure of original bone cells

facts.statement: Internal blood vessels within the bone of Scipionyx have been preserved, sometimes still appearing empty.
facts.quote: Also the internal blood vessels of the bone have been preserved, in some cases still empty inside

facts.statement: Six vertebrae in Scipionyx are capped by cartilaginous synchondroses, a feature typical of juveniles.
facts.quote: Six vertebrae are visibly capped by cartilaginous synchondroses, a typical juvenile feature

facts.statement: Cartilaginous caps are present on all limb joints of Scipionyx, including the smallest ones.
facts.quote: Cartilaginous caps are also present on all limb joints, even the smallest

facts.statement: The tracheal rings of Scipionyx have an average length of 0.33 millimeters and are separated by 0.17-millimeter-thick interspaces.

facts.statement: The preserved trachea of Scipionyx is quite thin, with a width of one millimeter.

facts.statement: Biliverdine, a bile component expected in the liver, was present in the preserved tissues of Scipionyx.
facts.quote: Also biliverdine was present, a bile component expected in the liver

facts.statement: A 2011 study reinterpreted a feature previously seen as a reduced hyposphene-hypantrum complex as a pair of tendon attachment points.
facts.quote: it was by the 2011 study seen as a pair of attachment points for tendons, as identified in 2006 in Compsognathus

facts.statement: The backward position of the prey bone cluster suggests Scipionyx had a dual stomach structure with a proventriculus and a muscular gizzard.

facts.statement: The fossil preserves no traces of skin, scales, or feathers.
